title: Matched-H training: is the large-H loss a representation problem or a training problem?
question: F0's two readings of the retrieval ceiling were not separated by the original design: does the representation degrade with the population, or was the router trained at 8 candidates so the sweep measures transfer? Train and evaluate at matched H and find out.
hypothesis: H_rep: the large-H loss is a property of the scoring representation — the basis cannot express the relevance relation at large populations. H_train: the loss is a property of the training population — matched-H training recovers the large-H signal. The pre-committed rule expected exactly one to hold.

arms.name: matched
arms.intervention: train and evaluate at the same candidate count, at every H
arms.schedule: 500 training steps at the matched H, for every H

endpoints.name: routing@1
endpoints.role: the primary endpoint — the trained-state diagonal
endpoints.description: Argmax accuracy at evaluation from raw dot products, with the router trained at the H it is evaluated at. The reproduction reference for F2 and F3.

endpoints.name: delta_1
endpoints.description: The analytic-vector reference reaches delta_1 ~= +3.07 at every H, which is what proves the basis is adequate.

decision_rule.condition: matched-H training recovers the large-H signal
decision_rule.licenses: H_train is supported and H_rep refuted: the loss is a training-population property, and the retrieval index (M2.1, historically Stage F1) builds on a representation that is adequate at the population it is trained for.
decision_rule.does_not_license: that the representation is adequate at populations it was never trained at.

decision_rule.condition: matched-H training does not recover the signal and the analytic vector also fails
decision_rule.licenses: H_rep is supported: the basis cannot express the relation at large H, and the architecture, not the training, is the constraint.
decision_rule.does_not_license: that the training rule is unimplicated — the two hypotheses are not exhaustive, and a third reading is possible.

held_constant: the feature basis, the environment, the candidate generator and the evaluator are unchanged
the analytic vector — one shared untrained weight vector — is the reference that proves the basis is adequate at every H
no arm inherits another arm's weights
the model-state integrity gate runs before every measurement
status: run — neither pre-committed branch fired; the third reading is the result
result_note: Matched-H training is the worst row at every evaluation population, including its own: routing@1 0.6240 -> 0.3860 (8), 0.1900 -> 0.1300 (64), 0.0640 -> 0.0740 (256). The representation is not inadequate: the analytic vector reaches routing@1 = 1.0000 at H in {8,64,256,512} with delta_1 ~= +3.07, because basis_size never depends on the candidate count. The failure is in the learning dynamics — reward scarcity under REINFORCE at large H: 5 successes in 500 steps at H=256 against a 0.39% chance rate. The experiment was designed to choose an architecture and answered that the architecture is not the problem.
